sentences.text: In a double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized controlled trial involving 120 patients with chronic pain, participants received at-home transcranial electrical stimulation, either direct current aimed at the motor cortex or alternating current aimed at the prefrontal cortex.

Researchers measured pain sensitivity using quantitative sensory tests for pressure and heat thresholds, pain modulation, and temporal summation, checking the effects immediately after treatment and again after six months.
Statistical analysis showed no significant changes in the pain test scores after the stimulation at any time point.
Consequently, the results do not support the idea that the pain relief from this stimulation comes from changes in how the brain modulates pain.
The authors suggest that future studies should check if these specific pain tests are sensitive enough to detect any changes caused by the stimulation.
